10 — Overview ​

How invocation works. Read this before you write code.

Invocation is text substitution, not a tool call ​

A tool call is the model's decision. A skill invocation is the person's: they type /deploy staging, and the agent expands it before the model sees anything.

  typed:   /deploy staging eu-west
  sent:    Check the tests pass, then deploy to staging in eu-west.

Three consequences:

  1. The model never sees the shorthand. It sees instructions, which is what it can act on.
  2. Expansion happens before the session records the turn. A resumed run replays what was sent, not the shorthand.
  3. An unknown name is passed through. Deleting the person's text because of a typo is worse than sending a slash command the model ignores.

Placeholders ​

Two forms, often in one body:

PlaceholderReplaced with
$ARGUMENTSeverything after the skill name, as one string
$0, $1, $2one whitespace-separated word, by position
$9 with no argumentthe empty string

Replace $ARGUMENTS first. Both forms start with $, and a positional pass that runs first can corrupt the longer token.

  args:  staging eu-west
  "Deploy to $0 in $1. Full: $ARGUMENTS"
  → "Deploy to staging in eu-west. Full: staging eu-west"

Arguments are split on whitespace. Quoting inside an argument is not handled, and this page says so rather than implying otherwise.

Stacking ​

One prompt can name several skills. Arguments run from the skill name to the next slash command:

  "/review /deploy production eu-west"

  review  → arguments: ""                    (nothing before the next command)
  deploy  → arguments: "production eu-west"

Expansion walks left to right and preserves order, because the order is the instruction. "Review, then deploy" and "deploy, then review" are different jobs.

The catalogue is already there ​

Chapter 09 handles discovery and advertisement. This chapter adds one method to the same Catalog, and one line in main before the prompt becomes history. The system message does not change, and neither does the loop.

What this chapter does not do ​

  • No scripts. A skill is instructions, not a bundled program.
  • No named arguments. Only $ARGUMENTS and positional.
  • No model-chosen invocation. The person types the command.

Self-check ​

  1. Who decides to invoke a skill: the model or the person? (Invocation is text substitution, not a tool call)
  2. Why is $ARGUMENTS replaced before $0? (Placeholders)
  3. How are arguments delimited when two skills share a prompt? (Stacking)
  4. What happens to a skill name that does not exist? (Invocation is text substitution, not a tool call)
  5. Which chapter does discovery, and which does expansion? (The catalogue is already there)
